headline: Approved Mestiza Latin Kitchen's restaurant license at 491 Dutton Street, 5-0; set September 3 hearings for Tesco Center and BonChon.
summary: Approved several event alcohol permits and one-day licenses, including for the Lowell Irish Festival and the Multicultural Festival. Approved a new restaurant license for Mestiza Latin Kitchen at 491 Dutton Street after a failed motion to continue the hearing. Approved the General On-Premises alcohol license type, 4-1, and continued the regulations hearing to September 3, 2026.
decisions: Approved special events permit for Salsa on the Deck, Sundays August 30 to October 18, 2026, 5-0.
Approved additional amplified entertainment permits and change to All Alcoholic Beverages licenses for the Lowell Summer Music Series at Boarding House Park, 5-0.
Approved one-day malt beverage and wine license and amplified entertainment permit for the 2026 Lowell Irish Festival on September 12, 2026, 5-0.
Approved one-day all alcoholic beverages license for the Multicultural Festival at JFK Plaza on September 12, 2026, 5-0.
Approved one-day malt beverage and wine license for The Town and The City Festival 3 on August 15, 2026, 5-0.
Approved three one-day malt beverage and wine licenses for UMass Lowell campus events on August 17, September 20, and September 24, 2026, 5-0.
Approved one-day wine and malt beverage license for a Christian Women Fellowship on August 23, 2026, at the Hellenic Center, 41 Broadway Street, 5-0.
Approved lodging house license for premises at 412 Fletcher Street, 5-0.
Approved common victualler license for Dip & Dine at 1290 Westford Street, 5-0.
Approved common victualler license for Nanna's Kitchen at 1040 Gorham Street, 5-0.
Motion to continue the Mestiza Latin Kitchen Corp. hearing to September 3, 2026, failed, 2-3.
Approved new Wine and Malt Beverages restaurant license for Mestiza Latin Kitchen Corp. at 491 Dutton Street, Unit 4, by unanimous roll call, 5-0.
Approved making the General On-Premises annual alcohol license type available to applicants in Lowell, pending conditions of license, 4-1.
Continued the public hearing on Lowell Alcoholic Beverages Regulations to September 3, 2026, 5-0.
Approved a September 3, 2026 compliance hearing for Tesco Center, 70-72 Middlesex Street, on a June 28, 2026 allegation under regulation 2.04, 5-0.
Approved a September 3, 2026 compliance hearing for Tesco Center, 70-72 Middlesex Street, on a July 26, 2026 allegation under regulations 1.06, 1.16, and 1.21, 5-0.
Approved holding a September 3, 2026 hearing at 6 PM on alteration of premises for BonChon Restaurant, 1075 Westford Street, 5-0.
Placed communications regarding incidents and events on file, 5-0.

Lowell License Commission | Meeting Minutes for 2026.08.13 
 
City of Lowell License Commission | 375 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA 01852  Page 1 of 6 
 
This meeting was held in City Council Chambers, second floor, City Hall, 375 Merrimack St. on 
Thursday, August 13, 2026, at 6:00 PM, and by Zoom invitation. 
Video of this meeting is available: https://www.youtube.com/live/QB3ZP6jYYcQ?si=skESmpOeIPaiGUmI 
 
ROLL CALL: 
On a roll call at 18:00, members present were, namely: Commission Chair Donahue, Commissioner Krieger, 
Commissioner Mercier, Commissioner Underwood, and Commissioner Uong. 
  
MINUTES:  
1 Acceptance of the meeting minutes for July 23, 2026.  
Move approval by Commissioner Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Underwood. 4 yeas, 1 
abstain (C. Uong), APPROVED. 
2 Application by Salsa in Lowell, François Chevalier, Owner, for a "Special Events Permit for Amplified 
Outdoor Public Entertainment," for ‘Salsa on the Deck,’ to be held on some Sundays  from August 30 
to October 18, from 2 to 5 PM at the DCR park located at 262 Merrimack Street. 
Mr. Chevalier spoke to the Commission about his return to “Salsa on the Deck.” 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Krieger. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
3 Application by James Macdonald for an additional  "Special Events Permits for Amplified Outdoor 
Public Entertainment," and to change the approved "Wines and Malt Beverages" licenses to "All 
Alcoholic Beverages" licenses for the remainder of the 36th Season of the ‘Lowell Summer Music 
Series’ at Boarding House Park, 40 French Street. Specifics listed below: 
• Retroactively: 
○ Sunday, August 2, "J. J. Grey & Mofro," 
○ Friday, August 7, "Iron & Wine," 
○ Saturday, August 8, "Christone 'Kingﬁsh' Ingram," 
○ Sunday, August 9, "Ripe," 
• Going Forward: 
○ Friday, August 14, "Watchhouse," 
○ Saturday, August 15, "Pink Talking Fish," 
○ Thursday, August 20, "The Record Company & Charlie Musselwhite," 
○ Friday, August 21, "Lotus Land," 
○ Sunday, August 30, "New England Film Orchestra," (new date) 
○ Friday, September 4, "Margo Price," 
○ Saturday, September 12, "45th Annual Banjo & Fiddle Contest," 
○ Sunday, September 13, "Graham Nash."
Lowell License Commission | Meeting Minutes for 2026.08.13 
 
City of Lowell License Commission | 375 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA 01852  Page 2 of 6 
 
Mr. Macdonald spoke to the Commission about the success of the Lowell Summer Music Series and 
how he wants to expand alcohol service to include canned mixed drinks like the popular seltzers. He 
also reviewed a new concert added to the series. 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Uong. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
4 Application by Peter Lally, Lo well Memorial Auditorium, for a "Special One Day License to 
sell/dispense Malt Beverages & Wines" and a "Special Events Permit for Amplified Outdoor Public 
Entertainment," for the 2026 Lowell Irish Festival. Event to be held on Saturday, September 12, 
2026, from Noon to 10 PM at Lowell Memorial Auditorium grounds, 50 East Merrimack Street. 
Mr. Lally appeared before the Commission in Council Chambers. He reviewed the plans for this, the 
7th or 8th Irish Festival organized by LMG Presents d/b/a Lowell Memorial Auditorium.  
Motion to approve by Commissioner Underwood; seconded by Commissioner Mercier. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
5 Application by Sheunesu Moyo, Dwelling House of  Hope, for a "Special One Day License for Non-
Profit to sell/dispense All Alcoholic Beverages"  for the Multicultural Festival on Saturday, September 
12, 2026, from 11 AM to 7 PM at JFK Plaza, 50 Arcand Drive. 
Mr. Moyo spoke to the Commission about his plans for the 4th annual Multicultural Festival, noting 
that he’s organized 3 of the annual events. He confirmed that LPD details were scheduled for the 
festival, and Lowell Police Captain Peaslee confirmed that there have been no prior incidents or 
issues during this festival. Commission Chair Donahue confirmed with the applicant that the four 
bartenders serving at the event are TIPS Certified.  
Motion to approve by Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Krieger. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
6 Application by Corey Belanger for a "Special On e Day License to sell/dispense Malt Beverages and 
Wines" for The Town and The City Festival 3 on Saturday, August 15, 2026, from 3 to 5 PM on Palmer 
Street. 
Mr. Belanger appeared before the board to speak about his event, third in a series of collaborations 
with the City of Lowell. He noted that he would like an extension to the hours of service on the 
application, due to the addition of another band to the event. He confirmed for the Commission that 
the event would have the same footprint as the prior two events this summer, and he confirmed 
Police Detail would be present and his bartenders are TIPS Certified.  
Motion to approve by Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Krieger. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED.
Lowell License Commission | Meeting Minutes for 2026.08.13 
 
City of Lowell License Commission | 375 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA 01852  Page 3 of 6 
 
7 Applications by Elizabeth Lopez for Aramark at Tsongas Center, for three "Special One Day Licenses 
to sell/dispense Malt Beverages and Wines only," for the following events on UMass Lowell's 
campus: 
• Monday, August 17, 2026, 5:00 to 7:00 PM for a "Paraprofessional to Teacher Gathering," Allen 
House, 2 Solomon Way. 
• Sunday, September 20, 2026, 2:30 to 5:30 PM for a "Field Hockey Alumni Day Celebration" 
reception, at Kennedy Family Athletics Center, 275 Riverside Street. 
• Thursday, September 24, 2026, 6:30 to 8:30 PM for the "Celebrating Careers in Law" reception, at 
Coburn Hall, 850 Broadway Street. 
Ms. Lopez reviewed her applications, noting that the University’s fall semester is getting started. 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Underwood. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
8 Application by Amanda Étinge, for a "Special One Day License to sell/dispense Wines and Malt 
Beverages only," for a "Christian Women Fellowship" on Sunday, August 23, 2026, from 1 PM to 10 
PM, at the Hellenic Center, 41 Broadway Street. 
Ms. Étinge spoke to the Commission via Zoom. She noted that this event was being moved to this 
venue due to a larger crowd (#100). She confirmed that her usual TIPS Certified bartenders would be 
serving. 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Uong. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
9 Application by 412 Realty Trust, Suzanne Donahue, Trustee, for Lodging House License for premises 
at 412 Fletcher Street. 
Ms. Donahue (no relation to Commission Chair Donahue) appeared before the Commission. She 
confirmed that all her permits with the City were approved.  
Motion to approve by Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Uong. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
10 Application by Lokesh Mohan, owner of Sh ree Vishnu Padmavati LLC [d/b/a] Dip & Dine, for 
Common Victualler license for 1290 Westford Street. 
M. Mohan spoke briefly about their restaurant concept and menut. 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Underwood. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
11 Application by Minhas Shaik, LLC Manager of Chinna and Minna LLC [d/b/a] Nanna's Kitchen, for 
Common Victualler license for 1040 Gorham Street. 
M. Shaik reviewed their business model, noting that the restaurant is exclusively “to go.”
Lowell License Commission | Meeting Minutes for 2026.08.13 
 
City of Lowell License Commission | 375 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA 01852  Page 4 of 6 
 
Motion to approve by Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Krieger. 5 yeas, 
APPROVED. 
12 Public hearing for an application by Mestiza La tin Kitchen Corp., Luisa Fernanda Lopera, proposed 
license manager, for a new "Wine and Malt Beverages" Restaurant license for 491 Dutton Street, 
Unit 4. 
Attorney Michael Zaim spoke for Mestiza Latin Kitchen, reviewing the applicant’s business plan and 
hope to expand their service with beer and wine. Atty. Zaim reviewed the proposed manager’s 
experience and how they proposed to control the service area.  
At the public hearing, no one spoke in favor of the application, however, several neighbors did speak 
in opposition (Peter Fisher, Tony Wallace, Mark Demello, Alves Aires). 
Commission Chair Donahue noted, in summary, that there seemed to be issues with the 
condominium association and communication problems between the 4 associations managing the 
mixed use building. He noted that the lease, granted by one of the owners and approved by the 
association, permitted alcohol in this restaurant area. Commissioner Donahue then asked Atty. Zaim 
to provide suggestions for mitigating various concerns voiced.  
Motion to continue hearing at September 3, 2026, meeting by C. Krieger, seconded by C. Uong. 
Motion lost 3 to 2 on a roll-call vote: C. Donahue – N; C. Krieger – Y; C. Mercier – N; C. Underwood 
– N; C. Uong – Y; 2 yeas, 3 nays. 
Commission Chair Donahue clarified the expectation that the applicant use signage and physical 
controls in place to keep alcohol and patrons within the business footprint. 
Motion to approve the application by Commissioner Underwood; seconded by Commissioner 
Mercier. Passed unanimously on a roll-call vote: C. Donahue – Y, C. Krieger – Y, C. Mercier – Y, C. 
Underwood – Y, C. Uong – Y; 5 yeas, APPROVED. 
13 Public Hearing to discuss Lowe ll Alcoholic Beverages Regulations. 
At the hearing, City Councilor Rita Mercier spoke, in their capacity as a resident of the City, in favor 
of the proposed regulations, noting that an unintended loophole in the regulations had allowed 
minors to be invited into one of the bars downtown. City Councilor McDonough also spoke, in their 
capacity as a resident of the City, in favor of the proposed regulations, noting that the proposed 
changes would not affect the majority of the restaurants and bars who already have policies in place 
to manage underage patrons. Some business owners also spoke regarding the proposed regulations: 
P. Hamourgas of the Worthen, N. Petrakos of Blue Shamrock, and E. Lugo of Tesco Center, each 
offered opinions and comments.  
Solicitor Wood reviewed the proposed regulatory changes and their purpose. Discussion included an 
overview of the history of alcohol regulations in the City of Lowell, the effectiveness of past violation 
hearings and their decisions, and methods used by comparable municipalities to reduce underage 
drinking and other alcohol-related illegalities. The Commission commented on the proposals and

chose to enact the first part: approving the “General On-Premises” license type, and noting that 
restrictions on the license type would be determined during the continuation of the hearing, along 
with the other proposed regulatory changes. [Draft Transcript of this hearing is attached to these 
minutes.] 
Motion to approve and make the “General On-Premises” type of annual alcohol license available 
to applicants in the City of Lowell, pending enumeration and vote on conditions of license, made 
by Commissioner Mercier and seconded by Commissioner Underwood. Passed on a roll-call vote: 
C. Donahue – Y, C. Krieger – N, C. Mercier – Y, C. Underwood – Y, C. Uong – Y; 4 yeas, 1 nay.  
Motion to continue the hearing at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting by 
Commissioner Uong; seconded by Commissioner Mercier. 5 yeas, APPROVED. 
14 Communication dated August 5,  2026, from Lowell Police Superintendent, Gregory Hudon, regarding 
allegations of misconduct charged against Picante Entertainment Group Inc. [d/b/a] Tesco Center, 
70-72 Middlesex Street, Ernesto Lugo, License Manager, all alcoholic beverages restaurant licensee. 
Allegations of misconduct occurred June 28, 2026, regarding failure to comply with Alcoholic 
Beverages Regulations for Licenses Issued by the Lowell License Commission, specifically 2.04. 
Request for a compliance hearing to be held at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting. 
Motion to hold a compliance hearing at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting by 
Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Underwood. 5 yeas, APPROVED. 
15 Communication dated August 5,  2026, from Lowell Police Superintendent, Gregory Hudon, regarding 
allegations of misconduct charged against Picante Entertainment Group Inc. [d/b/a] Tesco Center, 
70-72 Middlesex Street, Ernesto Lugo, License Manager, all alcoholic beverages restaurant licensee. 
Allegations of misconduct occurred July 26, 2026, regarding failure to comply with Alcoholic 
Beverages Regulations for Licenses Issued by the Lowell License Commission: 1.06, 1.16, and 1.21. 
Request for a compliance hearing to be held at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting. 
Motion to hold a compliance hearing at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting by 
Commissioner Mercier; seconded by Commissioner Underwood. 5 yeas, APPROVED. 
16 Request for a hearing for an application by Ta keo LLC, [d/b/a] BonChon Restaurant, Victor Vang, 
license manager, for alteration of premises of an "All Alcoholic Beverages" restaurant license for 
premises at 1075 Westford Street. It is requested that legal notice be published in local newspaper, 
and public hearing to be held on September 3, 2026, at 6 PM. 
Motion to hold a hearing at the September 3, 2026, License Commission meeting by Commissioner 
Krieger; seconded by Commissioner Mercier. 5 yeas, APPROVED. 
17 Communications to Commission regarding incidents and events. 
Motion to place the matters on file by Commissioner Donahue, seconded by Commissioner 
Mercier. 5 yeas, APPROVED.
Lowell License Commission | Meeting Minutes for 2026.08.13 
 
City of Lowell License Commission | 375 Merrimack St. Lowell, MA 01852  Page 6 of 6 
 
ADJOURNMENT: 
Commissioner Krieger made a motion to adjourn at 20:08, seconded by Commissioner Mercier.  
5 yeas, APPROVED.
